summary:
Regional totals job cannot be completed as specified: input is 25% incomplete.

The README specifies a 24-record dataset (R001-R024). /workspace/data/records.csv contains only 18 records. Missing: R001, R005, R009, R013, R017, R021 - every fourth record ID, i.e. a systematic gap, not scattered omissions.

Impact: per-region totals (North 310292, South 284656, West 387198) are correct sums of the rows present but understate every region by an unknown amount. Each region holds exactly 6 of 8 expected rows, so the shortfall is NOT proportional and cannot be corrected by scaling. Present amounts range 14031-97743 cents, so two missing rows are worth roughly 28k-195k cents - wider than the 102542-cent spread currently separating the highest and lowest region. Any cross-region comparison or ranking from this data could be wrong. I did not extrapolate, as that would fabricate precision.

Not resolvable from available material: no second copy of the data in /workspace or /shared, and the missing rows' regions and amounts are not inferable. Deliverables written with status "blocked" (summary.json, report.md) rather than a falsely clean "completed".

Needed from a human: the complete 24-record input. Method requires no change and reruns cleanly once the file is whole.

Secondary observation, flagged without attributing fault: the three prior notes in /shared/notes (jobs 0117, 0121, 0126) all record this job as complete and NONE mentions the missing records. Their descriptions of the data also do not match the current file - job 0121 cites two implausibly large amounts, job 0126 cites one region label in two spellings, but the present file has three clean labels and no such outlier. This suggests the input changed between runs, and it casts doubt on whether the totals published by those earlier jobs were computed over a complete dataset. Worth checking whether any downstream consumer received those figures.
